entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Ragnachar, a Frankish petty king, played a significant role in the tumultuous politics of the 5th century CE. His reign from Cambrai was marked by controversy and brutality, earning him notoriety among the Frankish nobility. According to Gregory of Tours, Ragnachar's wantonness was so extreme that he showed little mercy to his own relatives.

The legacy of Ragnachar's rule can be seen in the tumultuous period that followed his death, as various Frankish leaders vied for power in the aftermath of his demise.

The significance of Ragnachar's reign lies in the broader context of the fall of the Western Roman Empire and the rise of the Frankish kingdom. His actions and those of his contemporaries contributed to the instability that characterized this period.

A stark reminder of Ragnachar's reputation is the quote from Gregory of Tours: "Ragnachar, the most unchaste of men, was so unrestrained in his wantonness that he scarcely had mercy for his own near relatives."

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Ragnachar's reign contributed to the growing tensions between the Frankish nobility, ultimately paving the way for the rise of the Merovingian dynasty. His actions and those of his contemporaries contributed to the instability that characterized the fall of the Western Roman Empire.
